title: Delta classifier & routing playbook for Responses -> OpenAI mapping gaps
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: build a lightweight delta-classifier that identifies and scores behavioral and schema gaps between Redwood's Responses mapping and the OpenAI Responses API, plus an automated routing/playbook that selects an appropriate mitigation (proxy, degrade, or strict-fail) per request. Scope covers streaming event shapes, tool/function-call handoff semantics, structured output schema fidelity, and event ordering/stream termination edge cases. Deliverables: classifier logic, test harness, telemetry signals, routing policies, canary rollout plan, and acceptance criteria. Rationale: we see frequent customer bugs and subtle regressions when migrating from OpenAI to Redwood or vice versa; this work reduces surprise failures and gives customers predictable compatibility behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: Delta-classifier detects at least 95% of pre-labeled gap cases in the training corpus (precision >= 0.9 for high-severity categories)
Routing playbook supports three actions: pass-through proxy, best-effort degradation with documented lossiness, and strict contract reject; each action has an automated fallback
End-to-end test harness reproduces representative streaming/toolcall/structured-output regressions with deterministic fixtures
Telemetry dashboards show per-route gap rate, average gap severity, and post-mitigation success metrics
Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic with metric gates defined (error-rate delta, latency delta, customer-facing failures)
decision_log: 2025-01-22 - Decided to classify gaps into taxonomy: schema-mismatch, event-order, partial-stream, toolcall-contract, semantic-lossiness; prioritized schema-mismatch and toolcall-contract for Phase 1 - Asha
2025-01-24 - Chose to implement classifier as a small stateless service (Python) that evaluates request/response events against rules + ML heuristics; fast-path rule engine for known patterns - Marco
2025-01-28 - Agreed routing actions: PASS (proxy), DEGRADE (best-effort with lossiness header and structured warnings), FAIL (strict reject); DEGRADE requires explicit telemetry tagging - Priya

2025-02-02 - Opted to keep transformation logic out of the runtime hot path; router will return a candidate action and the serving runtime will apply transformations asynchronously when possible - Ethan
test_plan: Create labelled corpus: 1k synthetic conversations + 300 real repros from support (streaming/toolcall/structured outputs)
Unit tests for rule-engine: 200 cases covering event shapes and ordering variations
Integration harness: replay streams through proxy vs. direct runtime and compare semantics; measure delta in token streams and toolcall invocations
Canary tests: run against shadow traffic for 72h before enabling active routing; monitor regressions and false positives
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (shadow): deploy classifier & router in shadow mode for 7 days; collect signals and tune thresholds
Stage 1 (canary): enable 'DEGRADE' action for 5% traffic on non-critical orgs; monitor metric gates for 48h
Stage 2 (expanded canary): 25% traffic with automated rollback gates; manual review of customer-impacting events
Stage 3 (ga): default to PASS for gold-tier customers unless explicitly requested; enable DEGRADE for self-serve customers with opt-out
